candidates.title: Build a post-purchase second-order flow for first-time buyers
candidates.hypothesis: Only 20-27% of first-time Babyshop buyers in SE/NO/FI (10-12% in DK) order again within 180 days, and 38% of those second orders land inside the first 30 days. Voyado has Welcome, Abandoned Cart, Activation and Reactivation automations but nothing triggered by a first purchase, so new buyers only get the bulk campaign calendar in the window where a second order is most likely. Subscribed one-order customers reorder ~50% more often than unsubscribed or never-contacted ones, so email reach does move this metric.
candidates.action: CRM builds a 3-step Voyado automation triggered by first delivered order (day 3 care/fit + complementary category, day 14 next-need by entry category, day 30 incentive only for non-returners), branched by entry category - bikes/toys buyers get a bridge into outdoor clothing and shoes. Run with a Voyado control group from day one.

candidates.replication: Second-order rates hold in two cohorts (2025Q4 and 2026Q1) and in all four Nordic markets; the entry-category gap holds in both cohorts; the subscribed vs non-subscribed gap holds in each market separately (SE 32.2/22.4/20.9%, NO 23.8/16.6/15.3%, FI 24.3/14.0/15.1%, DK 14.9/8.7/7.4% for subscribed/unsubscribed/non-contact, customers of any prior order count).

sizing.baseline_note: Monthly GP2 from second orders placed within 180 days of the first order, Babyshop SE/NO/FI/DK, Q3 2026 average: net revenue from fct_customer_orders (order_seq_observed=2, days_since_prev_order<=180) = SE 1.390M, NO 0.709M, FI 0.233M, DK 0.137M, each multiplied by that market's Babyshop GP2 margin for Q3 2026 from agg_daily_profit_ladder (ratio of sums: SE 25.67%, NO 22.55%, FI 19.64%, DK 18.40%). Assumes second orders carry the market-average GP2 margin.
sizing.uplift_rationale: The observed gap between subscribed and non-emailed one-order customers is +50% relative, but most of that is self-selection and the flow only reaches the ~70% who are subscribed. 6% more second orders is roughly one eighth of that gap; high case assumes the bikes/toys branch closes a third of its distance to apparel.

pilot.metric: 30-day and 90-day second-order rate of first-time buyers, flow vs Voyado control group
pilot.control: Randomised Voyado control group (20-30% of triggered contacts); SE/NO/DK same period as secondary control if run FI-only
pilot.decision_rule: Roll out if the treated group's 30-day second-order rate is at least 8% (relative) above control with the interval excluding zero. FI alone gives ~1,400 first-time buyers a month and ~100 second orders in 30 days, which cannot detect a 6% move - run the holdout in all four markets at once and read FI as one stratum.

candidates.risks: History only starts June 2025, so 'first order' means first observed order; the cohorts include some returning customers who were quiet for 4-6+ months, which inflates the base rate slightly. The Voyado message export may not show flows built in another tool (e.g. transactional mails carrying recommendations: 648k transactional sends exist and were not inspected). Uplift is not measured. FI-specific: the EUR 129 free-shipping threshold and SEK/10 pricing make a small second basket less attractive in Finland, so FI may under-respond.
candidates.curator_note: Second-order rates and the baseline revenue were re-queried by the curator and match. Finland alone cannot detect the base uplift, so the pilot is a contact-level holdout in all four markets with Finland read as one group.

candidates.title: Fire a next-size reminder to last season's outerwear and shoe buyers
candidates.hypothesis: Children outgrow outerwear and shoes every year: customers who do come back for outerwear a year later buy a size that is on average 12 cm larger. Yet only 18% of autumn-2025 outerwear buyers have returned for anything in the same weeks of 2026, and no automation uses the purchased size or the purchase anniversary - they only receive the general campaign calendar.
candidates.action: CRM builds a Voyado automation keyed on last year's purchase date and size for outerwear, boots, trainers, sandals and swimwear: 'X has probably grown out of size N - here is this season in size N+1/N+2', sent 2-3 weeks before the anniversary, with the same brand/model family first. Needs the purchased size (already in the Norce line name) exposed to Voyado.

candidates.hypothesis: The abandoned-cart automation only went live in July 2026 and immediately became the most productive mail per send (about 10 SEK attributed revenue per send against about 0.5 SEK for campaigns), but it is a single message. A second and third reminder reach people who did not open the first, at no media cost.
candidates.action: CRM adds step 2 (about 24 h, social proof / low-stock) and step 3 (about 72 h, free-shipping or small incentive only for non-buyers) to BS_AUT_AbandonedCart in all languages, with exit on purchase and a control group on the new steps.

evidence.claim: BS_AUT_AbandonedCart delivered 12 mails in May and 33 in June 2026, then 15,845 in July, 18,410 in August and 18,027 in September - it effectively launched 2 July 2026.
evidence.sql: /* old project */ select format_date('%Y-%m', deliveryDate) m, count(*) ac_deliveries, count(distinct d.contactId) contacts from voyado.deliveries d join voyado.marketing_messages m using(messageId) where m.messageName like '%AbandonedCart%' group by 1 order by 1

evidence.claim: Click-attributed orders from the flow: 165 orders / 168,717 SEK in July and 160 orders / 163,463 SEK for 1-26 August (receipt data ends 26 Aug) - about 10.6 SEK per delivered mail in both months.
evidence.sql: /* old project */ select format_date('%Y-%m', a.createdOnDate) m, case when m.messageName like '%AbandonedCart%' then 'AC' when m.messageName like '%Welcome%' then 'Welcome' when m.messageName like '%eactivation%' then 'Reactivation' when m.message_type='Automation' then 'other_auto' else 'campaign' end flow, count(*) orders, round(sum(a.revenue_sek)) rev from voyado.attributed_receipts a join voyado.marketing_messages m on m.messageId=a.attributed_messageId where a.is_email_attributed and a.createdOnDate>='2026-06-01' and not in_broken_fx_window group by 1,2 order by 2,1

evidence.claim: It is a single step: one message name and one workflow id; of 36,356 deliveries in Aug-Sep only 62 followed a previous cart mail to the same contact within 24 h and 1,775 within 1-4 days (repeat carts, not a sequence).
evidence.sql: /* old project */ with d as (select d.contactId, d.deliveryDateTime t, lag(d.deliveryDateTime) over(partition by d.contactId order by d.deliveryDateTime) p from voyado.deliveries d join voyado.marketing_messages m using(messageId) where m.messageName like 'BS_AUT_AbandonedCart%' and d.deliveryDate between '2026-08-01' and '2026-09-30') select count(*) n, countif(p is null) first_in_window, countif(timestamp_diff(t,p,hour)<=24) within24h, countif(timestamp_diff(t,p,hour) between 25 and 96) d1_4, countif(timestamp_diff(t,p,hour)>96) later from d; select count(distinct messageName) names, count(distinct workflowId) workflows from voyado.marketing_messages where messageName like 'BS_AUT_AbandonedCart%'

evidence.claim: Reach is uneven: deliveries per 30 days against GA4 users who added to cart without purchasing in September (sampled funnel) - SE ~8,350 mails vs ~21,000 abandoners (40%), NO ~2,610 vs ~10,100 (26%), FI ~930 vs ~3,560 (26%), DK ~580 vs ~4,220 (14%).
evidence.sql: /* old project */ select cm.market, count(*) deliveries, count(distinct d.contactId) contacts from voyado.deliveries d join voyado.marketing_messages m using(messageId) join voyado.contact_market cm using(contactId) where d.deliveryDate between '2026-07-10' and '2026-10-06' and m.messageName like 'BS_AUT_AbandonedCart%' and cm.market in ('SE','NO','FI','DK') group by 1; /* new warehouse */ select market, step_index, step_name, users, abandonments, sampled from babyshop_marts.agg_funnel_snapshots where is_current_version and breakdown='total' and scope_kind='market' and window_kind='d30' and window_end='2026-09-30' and market in ('SE','NO','FI','DK') and users>0 order by market, step_index

evidence.claim: In SE/NO/FI/DK between 1 June and 25 August 2026, automations were 2.8% of marketing sends (234,919 of 8.32M) but 15% of click-attributed email revenue (0.75M of 4.91M SEK): 3.2 SEK per send against 0.51 SEK for manual campaigns.
evidence.sql: /* old project */ select market, message_type, sum(sent) sent, sum(attributed_orders) ord, round(sum(attributed_revenue_sek)) rev from voyado.email_daily where event_date between '2026-06-01' and '2026-08-25' and market in ('SE','NO','FI','DK') group by 1,2 order by 2,1

candidates.replication: The flow's revenue per send was stable across its first two months (July 10.6 SEK, 1-26 August ~10.5 SEK) and it delivers in all four Nordic markets; the single-step structure is the same in every market since it is one workflow.

sizing.baseline_note: Monthly GP2 currently click-attributed to the abandoned-cart flow: July 168.7k SEK and August 163.5k for 26 days scaled to 195k for the month, average 182k SEK/month, times the all-market GP2 margin for Q3 2026 (23.8%, the Q3 baseline table in RULES.md). Voyado receipt revenue is treated as net; receipts stop on 2026-08-26 so September is not observed.
sizing.uplift_rationale: Outside rule of thumb: a second and third cart reminder typically add 30-50% to the first step's recovered revenue. Low case allows for the click-attributed baseline overstating incrementality.

candidates.risks: Baseline is last-click attribution, not incremental revenue - some of these carts would have converted anyway, and the flow has no control group. The FI figure is allocated by FI's 7.4% share of cart-mail deliveries. The reach comparison mixes mails with sampled GA4 users, so read the percentages as ordering, not levels. Base case is only just above the 10k floor.
candidates.curator_note: Only just above the floor, and the baseline is click-attributed revenue without a control group.

needs_data.hypothesis: Lekmer-only buyers get no CRM at all and could be bridged into Babyshop: 25,905 of 45,928 Nordic Lekmer customers have never bought on Babyshop and only 1,905 of them exist in Voyado; yet 11-13% of new Lekmer customers place a first Babyshop order within 180 days unprompted (Dec 2025-Mar 2026 cohorts).
needs_data.missing_source: Whether Lekmer runs its own email platform (no Lekmer-named message exists in the Voyado export), and the consent basis for mailing Lekmer buyers from Babyshop. Lekmer new-customer volume is also erratic (500-800/month Apr-Jul 2026, 3,200 in Sep), so the shop's status needs confirming.
needs_data.why_promising: Babyshop orders from customers whose first purchase was on Lekmer ran at 1.4-1.9M SEK/month in Q3 2026 (the early cohorts are inflated by pre-June-2025 Babyshop customers, so the true bridge is smaller). A recurring flow on ~1,200 Lekmer-only new buyers a month sizes below the floor on its own; a one-off mailing to the 24k stock could be worth more but is not a monthly figure.

needs_data.hypothesis: Bulk campaign email is incremental and frequency could be tuned by measured lift rather than attributed clicks.
needs_data.missing_source: Voyado deliveries before 2026-05-19. The only control groups in the export are from the July-August 2025 Superweek campaigns (about 5,000 SE contacts held out across seven sends, 71,984 control rows), but deliveries start in May 2026 so the treated recipients of those sends cannot be identified. A fresh control group on current campaigns would fix this.
needs_data.why_promising: Campaigns are 97% of sends and 85% of attributed email revenue (SE/NO/FI/DK, June-25 Aug 2026); a measured lift would also turn the subscribed vs non-subscribed gaps used in this lens from correlation into a causal number.

needs_data.hypothesis: Browse-abandonment and back-in-stock triggers would add to the triggered-mail revenue.
needs_data.missing_source: Whether Voyado web tracking / product-view events are captured per contact (no browse event table in the export), and stock-notification sign-ups.
needs_data.why_promising: The cart flow shows ~10 SEK per send from launch; product-view audiences are several times larger than cart audiences (SE: 165k item viewers vs 32k cart adders in September).

needs_data.hypothesis: Voyado receipt and attribution data stopped on 2026-08-26, so September-October email revenue (including the first Kuling winter campaigns) cannot be read.
needs_data.missing_source: voyado.receipts / receipt_items sync - the sync_state shows 0 new rows since about 22 September and the last receipt date is 26 August.
needs_data.why_promising: Every email sizing above leans on attributed receipts; campaign_performance shows 0 attributed orders for all September campaigns only because of this gap.

needs_data.hypothesis: First-order category should steer acquisition bidding: coverall/outerwear/trainer entrants are worth 300-380 SEK of repeat revenue in 180 days against 131 SEK for bike entrants.
needs_data.missing_source: Acquisition cost and channel per first-order category (new-customer orders joined to paid click source), which sits with the paid-media lens.
needs_data.why_promising: Bikes/balance bikes/scooters are the third largest entry category (11,307 first orders in six months) with half the 180-day repeat rate of apparel; if they are bought with the same tROAS the true return on them is lower than it looks.
